synthesis.p0_now:
Two independent crash surfaces, both HIGH, both defeat a safety net that was explicitly built. Ship both today.

P0-1 — Restore the crash-safety net for training runs (the supervisor is blind to Rust panics).
  - scripts/train_game.py:673 — the supervisor loop has only `except KeyboardInterrupt` (670) + `except Exception` (673). pyo3 0.22 converts a Rust panic to `pyo3_runtime.PanicException`, which subclasses BaseException, so `except Exception` cannot catch it. Any panic in Worker::step exits the process with ZERO restarts — exactly the "crashed and stayed dead" incident that 14010eb (shipped 1 day ago) was built to prevent, and it fires for 100% of prod configs.
  - FIX (three parts, all P0):
    (a) train_game.py:673 — add `except BaseException` after the KeyboardInterrupt arm (or catch PanicException by name off the nes_core module) so panics get the same restart-with-resume + backoff treatment. Every trainer-side `except Exception` guard has the same blind spot; broaden the ones wrapping pool.step_all / load_worker_state fallbacks.
    (b) Keep `catch_unwind` UNCONDITIONAL in step_all_native (pool.rs:1411-1420). Today with `panic_isolation:false` (trainer.py:2173, set by all 31 game configs) the code runs `Ok(work())` with no catch_unwind, so the dead-worker mark (pool.rs:1423-1435) and reset_all revival (pool.rs:751) never engage. Demote the flag to logging-verbosity only; measured cost of always-on was 0.5-1%.
  - Evidence: Cargo.toml:179 `panic="unwind"`; rayon pool (pool.rs:333) sets no panic_handler so it propagates; grep of src/training/*.py finds no `except BaseException`/`except PanicException` anywhere.

P0-2 — Guard NESEnvironment state-restore so the GUI/eval cannot hard-crash on a stale or wrong-game save-state.
  - nes_core/src/python.rs:220 (constructor NCST branch) and python.rs:467 (load_state) call `nes.apply_state(&state)` with NO catch_unwind — unlike the Pool equivalents (pool.rs:1185, pool.rs:1598) which were hardened after the 2026-04-21 wrong-game-state process-kill incident and cite it in comments. A bincode-valid blob with wrong-length `ram` panics in copy_from_slice (nes.rs:624); a same-format state from a different mapper panics "Invalid mapper state enum variant" (mapper/mapper0.rs:136). The deserialize calls just above (python.rs:213/462) already return PyValueError, but the panic lives inside apply_state, so those guards don't help.
  - Blast radius confirmed: GUI file picker (main_window.py:421, filter offers "All files (*)") feeds replay_window.py:100-104 `NESEnvironment(start_state_path=...)`, and that call sits OUTSIDE the try (and Exception couldn't catch PanicException anyway). A user picking a stale .state.bin hard-crashes the play window — the most visible "unprofessional" failure a customer can hit.
  - FIX: wrap apply_state at python.rs:220, python.rs:467, and python.rs:311 (reset_no_advance) in `catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(..))` → PyValueError with the "state not compatible with this ROM" guidance the Pool already emits; on failure leave the env cold-reset, not half-mutated. Then wrap the replay_window constructor call in a user-facing dialog.
synthesis.p1_this_week:
Eval integrity is the user's non-negotiable value and the go/no-go gate is Sunday — these three touch published numbers and receipt honesty.

P1-1 (medium, CONFIRMED) — seq_clear / worlds_cleared latch on ANY castle clear with no world or warp guard.
  - smb_sequential.py:152-157 sets `_seq_clear=True` + increments `_worlds_cleared` on any world-byte increment out of an x-4 castle, never checking the crossing left World 1; `_warp_taken` (157) is an independent latch that never vetoes it. Consumers latch unguarded: composite_policy.py:807 (`seq_clear_rate`, THE campaign metric), :702/:711 (worlds_cleared break), eval_game.py:481/494. An honest-eval episode that warps out of 1-2 and later clears a World-4 castle is counted as a sequential World-1 clear. The property docstring (smb_sequential.py:176 "crossing into World 2") is already contradicted by the code.
  - Also: `_per_level_breakdown` (composite_policy.py:757) counts exit_reason "advanced" as "cleared"; a warp out of 1-2 raises _label_rank so reason="advanced" (line 507), inflating per-level clears for levels the agent warped past.
  - FIX: gate the castle-clear branch on `self._prev_world == 0`; expose and use `seq_clear and not warp_taken` in summarize's seq_clear_rate and eval_game's tally; in _per_level_breakdown distinguish a warp exit from a forward clear. Add an assertion that warp_rate>0 episodes cannot contribute to seq_clear_rate.

P1-2 (medium, PLAUSIBLE) — Action receipts omit the random start-jitter noops, so honest-eval receipts do not self-replay.
  - composite_policy.py:650-652 runs `_rng.randint(0, start_jitter+1)` noop steps BEFORE recording begins (recording is only inside the control loop, 671-674); the meta sidecar (733) stores the configured MAX jitter and `steps=len(_recorded)`, not the drawn count. For the flagship `--sticky-prob 0.25 --start-jitter 16 --record-actions` config, a replayed .npy is phase-shifted by the unrecorded draw (seed-0 draws 14 noops) and does not reproduce its trajectory. emit_fm2.py:65 anchors at power-on with no jitter prefix, compounding it. This falsifies the unqualified Tier-A "all receipts self-replay / byte-compare" claim (memo:74, campaign:648) for every jitter>0 receipt.
  - FIX (either): append `_recorded.append(0)` per jitter noop when record_dir is set so the .npy is the complete stepped sequence; OR store the drawn count in meta and have replay/emit_fm2 prepend it. Add a receipt self-replay test with start_jitter>0 — there is currently NO receipt self-replay test at all. Until it passes, qualify the Tier-A claim in the campaign docs to "deterministic (jitter 0) receipts only".

P1-3 (low, but cheap + prevents data loss) — one off-map episode aborts the whole eval batch and loses the log row.
  - composite_policy.py:460 `_select` raises KeyError when resolve_level_key returns None; eval_composite.py:228-240 wraps the loop in `try/finally` with no `except`, and summarize()+the eval.jsonl append (244, 282-283) run AFTER the loop, so a mid-episode KeyError discards all N episodes and writes no row. Not reachable under shipped manifests (all carry `default`), but the blast radius is the real defect.
  - FIX: per-episode try/except in the eval loop recording an `off_map_level` result instead of aborting; and flush eval.jsonl incrementally (write-as-you-go) so a crash never discards completed episodes.
synthesis.p2_polish:
Latent hardening gaps and dead knobs — real inconsistencies worth closing, none firing under shipped configs today.

P2-1 (low) — RewardFunction.compute / compute_rewards_batch never validate RAM length.
  - python.rs:838 / python.rs:906 pass caller bytes straight into rewards.rs, which indexes fixed addresses unchecked (rewards.rs:1293 `ram[0x07DE..0x07E4]`, $075A/$0760 at 1322-1325). The sibling extract_smb_tiles/_v2 (python.rs:940/958) DO guard `>= 0x0800`; the reward path does not. Production always ships full 2048-byte RAM (pool.rs:1315/1336), so no live trigger — but it is an asymmetric-validation gap on a public PyO3 API.
  - FIX: `bytes.len() >= 0x0800` check → PyValueError at both entry points, same message shape as extract_smb_tiles.

P2-2 (low) — Audio render callback does `state.lock().unwrap()` inside the CoreAudio extern "C" frame.
  - audio.rs:426. If any lock-holder ever panics, the poisoned mutex turns the next callback's unwrap into a process SIGABRT (no traceback, no supervisor). No reachable poison origin exists today (all lock-holding sections are bounds-checked, index only after an early-return), but the codebase already defends this exact hazard elsewhere: pool.rs:1476/1492 use `lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner())`.
  - FIX: adopt the poison-recovering pattern for every lock in audio.rs (426, 256/281/289/300/320/366) and wrap fill_callback's body in catch_unwind that zero-fills `out`, so the callback can never unwind into CoreAudio.

P2-3 (low) — _gx_pad not cleared on a committed hysteresis level switch.
  - composite_policy.py:526-529 (the else-branch, incoming noop_pad==0) resets _gx_stage/_gx_confirm but leaves a stale `_gx_pad>0`, which would leak noop actions into the incoming specialist's first frames. Unreachable under shipped configs (2-1 is the only gx-routed level and its successor 2-2 carries an entry pad, taking the overwrite branch), but a future config with a gx switch near an auto-advance seam feeding a no-pad successor would trip it.
  - FIX: set `self._gx_pad = 0` in the level-switch commit branch before the pad check (the switch is authoritative). Add a state-machine test firing a hysteresis switch while _gx_pad>0.

P2-4 (low) — RustPool `seed` is a dead knob.
  - rust_pool_adapter.py:98 stores self._seed; start() (151-156) never passes it and nes_core.Pool::new (pool.rs:640-648) has no seed param; torch.manual_seed(seed) (eval_composite.py:121) is inert for greedy argmax. Reproducibility is actually intact (fixed save-state + greedy; the sticky/jitter _rng at composite_policy.py:643 IS correctly seeded), so this is a clarity/provenance smell, not a break — same class the audit priors flagged (eval --start-state, sticky_action_prob dead in vanilla_ppo).
  - FIX: either wire seed to a real emulator RNG or drop the `seed=` param from RustPool and rename the logged field to make clear it governs only the stochastic-eval RNG.
synthesis.systemic_patterns:
Five findings collapse into three structural root causes; each has one change that kills the whole class.

PATTERN A — The FFI panic boundary is enforced ad-hoc, not by contract (findings 1, 2, 3, 4).
  Rust panics cross into Python as PanicException (a BaseException subclass), which either (i) evades every `except Exception` guard, or (ii) aborts the process outright when the panic originates in an extern "C" frame (audio). The codebase hardened SOME sites reactively — pool.rs apply_state (1185/1598) and pool locks (1476/1492) after the 2026-04-21 incident — but NESEnvironment.apply_state, RewardFunction.compute, and the audio callback were never brought under the same rule, and the Python supervisor still only catches Exception.
  STRUCTURAL FIX (one contract, both sides): (1) Rust — every #[pymethods] entry point that touches emulator state or indexes caller buffers is wrapped in `catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(..))` → PyValueError via ONE shared macro/helper, so a new entry point cannot be added without the guard. (2) Python — the supervisor and all trainer guards catch BaseException (or PanicException by name), never bare Exception, for anything downstream of an FFI call. (3) Make catch_unwind unconditional (panic_isolation → logging verbosity only) so a panicking worker always degrades to dead+zero-frame instead of killing the run. This single boundary contract closes findings 1-4 at once.

PATTERN B — State-restore and public buffers are trusted without validation (findings 2, 3; echoes the load_worker_state history in project memory).
  Untrusted/mismatched save-states and short RAM buffers reach unchecked slice/enum operations that panic. Guarding is scattered per-caller.
  STRUCTURAL FIX: a single `validated_apply_state` (checks ram length + mapper variant, catch_unwind, leaves env cold-reset on failure) that ALL restore sites route through — constructor, load_state, reset_no_advance, pool — with no bypass; and a length-check helper on every pymethod that indexes fixed RAM addresses. Add one fuzz test that throws empty/truncated/wrong-game inputs at every public entry point and asserts PyValueError, never process death.

PATTERN C — Eval metrics and receipts latch/route on a partial view of state (findings 5, 6, 7, 8).
  seq_clear latches without a world/warp guard; receipts omit the jitter prefix; hysteresis leaks _gx_pad; an off-map level raises instead of isolating — each computes a headline result or an artifact from incomplete provenance, and the campaign publishes those numbers as Tier-A.
  STRUCTURAL FIX (two invariants): (1) The receipt is the COMPLETE self-contained stepped sequence from the start-state (record jitter noops), enforced by a mandatory self-replay byte-compare test that fails the local `make test` if ANY receipt doesn't reproduce. (2) Headline metrics are computed from an explicit provenance record (world crossed, warp_taken, off_map) with guards, and each episode runs inside its own try/except with incremental log flushing, so one bad episode can never falsify a metric, discard the batch, or lose the log row.

CROSS-CUTTING — Parsed-but-dead knobs (finding 9; priors: eval --start-state, sticky_action_prob in vanilla_ppo). STRUCTURAL FIX: a "no dead knobs" rule — every documented CLI/config parameter must be wired to observable behavior or removed, and logged provenance fields must reflect only what actually varied the run; a small test asserts each documented knob changes an output.
synthesis.professional_checklist:
Current state: the emulator core is strong and the crash-safety machinery EXISTS, but its guarantees have holes at the boundaries (Rust panics escape the net, one class of user action hard-crashes the GUI) and the eval layer publishes Tier-A claims that don't all hold. Concrete gap-to-shippable:

CRASH SAFETY (must-have before any customer runs it)
  [ ] Supervisor catches BaseException/PanicException, not just Exception — its entire stated job (train_game.py:673). VERIFY: kill a worker with a synthetic panic and confirm restart+resume, not process death.
  [ ] catch_unwind is unconditional in the pool step path; panic_isolation is logging-only. VERIFY: with the prod config (panic_isolation:false) a worker panic marks the worker dead and reset_all revives it.
  [ ] Every #[pymethods] entry touching emulator state or caller buffers is wrapped → PyValueError (NESEnvironment.apply_state x3, RewardFunction.compute x2, audio callback). Enforced by a shared macro so new entry points inherit it.
  [ ] Audio callback cannot abort the process: poison-recovering locks + catch_unwind zero-fill.

GUI ROBUSTNESS (customer-facing)
  [ ] Play-window Load State on a stale/wrong-game/corrupt .state.bin shows a dialog, never crashes (guard replay_window.py:100-104 + the underlying apply_state). VERIFY: pick a wrong-game state and a truncated file; both surface a clean message.
  [ ] File-picker filter stops offering "All files (*)" for state loads, or validates on load.

EVAL INTEGRITY (the user's non-negotiable value; Sunday go/no-go depends on it)
  [ ] seq_clear_rate gated on a real World-1→2 crossing AND not-warp; per-level breakdown distinguishes warp from clear; warp_rate cross-checked. The published campaign gate metric must not count a warp-then-later-world clear as a sequential World-1 clear.
  [ ] Every recorded receipt self-replays byte-for-byte from the start-state (jitter recorded; emit_fm2 jitter-aware), proven by a self-replay test in `make test`. Until green, the Tier-A "all receipts self-replay" claim in decision_memo/campaign docs is qualified to jitter-0 receipts.
  [ ] No eval batch is lost to one bad episode: per-episode try/except + incremental eval.jsonl flush.
  [ ] No dead knobs: audit seed (rust_pool_adapter.py:98), sticky_action_prob (dead in vanilla_ppo per memory), eval --start-state — wire or remove; logged provenance reflects only what varied the run.

TEST / PROCESS (local-first; no CI machinery per user preference)
  [ ] New regression test per fix: FFI-boundary fuzz (bad state / short RAM / wrong-game) asserting PyValueError; receipt self-replay with jitter>0; seq_clear warp-guard unit test; off-map-episode isolation test.
  [ ] All fixes verified end-to-end by reproducing each failure BEFORE the fix and confirming the guarded behavior after (reproduce → fix → re-run harness → hand off), then `make check` / `make test` / `make parity` green locally.
  [ ] Docs reconciled: any campaign/memo claim about receipt replayability or per-level clear rates is updated to match what the guarded code actually guarantees.

finding.title: The brand-new crash supervisor is blind to Rust worker panics: pyo3 PanicException subclasses BaseException and `except Exception` never catches it
finding.failure_scenario: With panic_isolation OFF (production default via `reinforce.panic_isolation: false`, applied at trainer.py:2173), any panic in Worker::step bypasses the catch_unwind at pool.rs:1411-1420 (`Ok(work())` at 1419), unwinds through rayon's join into Pool.step_all, and pyo3 0.22 raises `pyo3_runtime.PanicException` — which inherits from BaseException, not Exception. The supervisor loop shipped 1 day ago in 14010eb to prevent exactly the 'trainer crashed and stayed dead 2h' incident catches only `except Exception:` (train_game.py:673), and every trainer-side guard (`except Exception` around load_worker_state fallbacks, etc.) has the same blind spot. Concrete input: any finding-1 corrupt state, any mapper/PPU edge-case panic from the +862-line PPU churn — the process exits with an unhandled BaseException traceback, ZERO restarts, no auto-resume, no backoff; the run is dead until a human looks. The dead-worker isolation/revival machinery (pool.rs:1421-1436, reset_all revive at pool.rs:751) also never engages because the mark-dead code is skipped when the panic propagates.
finding.fix_sketch: In the supervisor loop, catch BaseException after the explicit KeyboardInterrupt arm (or catch PanicException by name: `import pyo3_runtime`-style attribute off the nes_core module) so Rust panics get the same restart-with-resume treatment as Python crashes. Separately, reconsider the isolation bypass: keep catch_unwind unconditionally in step_all_native (measured cost was 0.5-1%) and let the flag only control logging verbosity, so a panicking worker degrades to dead+zero-frame instead of killing the run.

verdict.reasons: Mechanism verified end-to-end. (1) train_game.py:670-673 has only `except KeyboardInterrupt` + `except Exception`; grep of src/training/*.py finds no `except BaseException`/`except PanicException` anywhere, so nothing catches a BaseException-derived error between pool.step_all and the supervisor. (2) Code default panic_isolation=True (trainer.py:925) but all 31 shipped game configs (mario*, smb_*, contra, zelda, metroid) set `panic_isolation: false`, and trainer.py:2173 pushes set_panic_isolation(False); OFF is the de-facto production default as claimed. (3) pool.rs:1411-1420 — with the flag off the code runs `Ok(work())` with NO catch_unwind; the `Err(_)` arm that sets `w.dead=true` (1423-1435) and the reset_all revival are only reachable via the catch_unwind branch, so the dead-worker isolation/revival machinery never engages, confirming the finding. (4) Cargo.toml:179 sets `panic = "unwind"` with a comment "panics become PyErr at the FFI boundary"; rayon ThreadPoolBuilder (pool.rs:333) sets no panic_handler so rayon propagates (not aborts) the panic to the collecting thread; it unwinds through step_all_native and py.allow_threads (pool.rs:817), and pyo3 0.22 (Cargo.toml:76) converts it to pyo3_runtime.PanicException, which pyo3 defines as a subclass of PyBaseException — not Exception. Therefore `except Exception` cannot catch it and the process dies with zero restarts, defeating the crash supervisor shipped in 14010eb. Severity lowered from critical to high: the finding slightly overstates the trigger — the most common corruption vector (bad save-state via load_worker_state) is separately guarded by its own catch_unwind at pool.rs:1185 returning a catchable PyValueError, so it does NOT hit this path. The genuine triggers are panics during Worker::step (RustedNES unimplemented-opcode/edge-case panic! branches noted in Cargo.toml, PPU/mapper indexing edge cases), which are uncommon under the validated-ROM/state precondition the flag assumes but real and fatal when they occur. Airtight defect defeating the explicit safety net for 100% of prod configs, but conditional on a step-panic event rather than firing on every input, hence high rather than critical.

finding.title: NESEnvironment.load_state and the constructor NCST path apply states unguarded — the exact panic class Pool was hardened against after the 2026-04-21 incident
finding.failure_scenario: python.rs:467 (`load_state`) and python.rs:220 (constructor `start_state_path` NCST branch) call `nes.apply_state(&state)` with NO catch_unwind, unlike the Pool equivalents (pool.rs:1185, pool.rs:1598) which were hardened after a wrong-game state killed the process. A bincode-valid blob with a wrong-length `ram` field (proven deserializable by pool.rs:1889-1917) panics in `copy_from_slice` at nes.rs:624; a same-format state saved from a different game/mapper panics with 'Invalid mapper state enum variant' (e.g. mapper0.rs:136). Callers are the GUI play-window Load State (user picks a stale .state.bin), eval/probe scripts, and single-env harvesters — they get an uncatchable-by-except-Exception PanicException instead of the clean PyValueError the Pool emits, crashing the eval run or the customer-facing GUI outright.
finding.fix_sketch: Mirror pool.rs: wrap both apply_state calls (python.rs:220 and python.rs:467, plus reset_no_advance's at python.rs:311) in `catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(..))` and convert the payload into a PyValueError with the same 'state not compatible with this ROM' guidance; on failure leave the env cold-reset rather than half-mutated.

verdict.reasons: All load-bearing claims verified against the code. python.rs:467 (load_state) and python.rs:220 (constructor NCST branch) both call nes.apply_state(&state) with no catch_unwind; the constructor's only catch_unwind (line 161) wraps just Nes::new(cart), not line 220. The deserialize calls preceding them ARE guarded and return PyValueError, but the panic risk lives inside apply_state, so those guards don't help. The Pool equivalents (pool.rs:1185, pool.rs:1598) DO wrap apply_state in catch_unwind→PyValueError, with comments explicitly citing the 2026-04-21 wrong-game-state process-kill incident — the asymmetry is exactly as described. Panic sources confirmed: nes.rs:624 self.ram.copy_from_slice(&state.ram) panics on ram-length mismatch, and mapper/mapper0.rs:136 (finding's path typo: mapper/ not mappers/) panics 'Invalid mapper state enum variant in apply_state'. The Pool test corrupt_state_blob_is_caught_not_unwound (pool.rs:1883-1924) proves a bincode-valid, ram-truncated blob deserializes cleanly then panics in apply_state. panic='unwind' is set (Cargo.toml:179), so PyO3 converts the panic to PanicException, which subclasses BaseException and is therefore NOT caught by 'except Exception' — matching the finding's core claim. Blast radius confirmed: the GUI file picker (main_window.py:421, filter even offers 'All files (*)') feeds the pick into replay_window.py:100-104's NESEnvironment(start_state_path=...) constructor, and that constructor call is outside the try/except Exception at line 109 (and Exception couldn't catch PanicException anyway); a user selecting a stale/wrong-game .state.bin hard-crashes the play flow. capture_start_state.py also calls load_state, and the only Python test on this path (test_state_roundtrip.py:103) exercises double-prefix stripping, not the mapper-mismatch/ram-length panic — no coverage. Minor scope trims that do not change the verdict: the third cited site, reset_no_advance (python.rs:311), only applies state when a start_state_snapshot was already loaded successfully via the constructor, so it is downstream of line 220 rather than an independent surface; and this is a bad-input robustness gap, not a happy-path or memory-safety crash, so it is high rather than critical. Severity high retained: uncatchable customer-facing GUI crash on a realistic user action, and the exact incident class the Pool was already hardened against.

finding.title: RewardFunction.compute / compute_rewards_batch never validate RAM length before rewards.rs indexes up to $07E4
finding.failure_scenario: `RewardFunction.compute` (python.rs:838) and `compute_rewards_batch` (python.rs:906) pass the caller's bytes straight into rewards.rs, which indexes fixed addresses unchecked — e.g. `&ram[0x07DE..0x07E4]` at rewards.rs:1293 and the SMB area/lives reads at $0760/$075A. The sibling entry points `extract_smb_tiles`/`extract_smb_tiles_v2` (python.rs:940, 958) explicitly reject buffers < 2048 bytes, but the reward path does not. Any Python-side caller that hands a sliced, empty, or sentinel RAM buffer (the (0,0)-sentinel substitution class from skip_preprocess mode, a harvester passing a stale view, a test passing b"") triggers an index-out-of-bounds panic that surfaces as PanicException — which, per finding 2, no supervisor or trainer guard catches.
finding.fix_sketch: At both entry points, check `bytes.len() >= 0x0800` and return PyValueError otherwise (same message shape as extract_smb_tiles). One comparison per call; the batch loop can hoist it per element before compute.

verdict.reasons:
The code-level fact is verified: RewardFunction.compute (python.rs:827-843) and compute_rewards_batch (python.rs:884-916) do NOT validate bytes.len() before passing to rewards.rs, which indexes fixed addresses unchecked (read_score ram[0x07DE..0x07E4] at rewards.rs:1293; $075A/$075C/$075F/$0760 at 1322-1325), whereas the sibling extract_smb_tiles/_v2 (python.rs:940/958) DO guard >=0x0800. A genuinely short buffer would panic. So a missing-guard / asymmetric-validation gap is real.

However the failure scenario is overstated and partly misread: (1) The cited skip_preprocess "(0,0)-sentinel substitution" applies only to the preprocessed/rgb frame buffers, never to RAM. Every worker-step branch in pool.rs ships RAM as full length — vec![0u8; RAM_SIZE=2048] (line 1315) or system_ram().as_ref().to_vec() (a fixed 0x0800 array, lines 1336/1408) — and build_result_list wraps it unconditionally via PyBytes::new_bound (line 1779). So r.ram_snapshot is invariant 2048 bytes; the sentinel never yields a short RAM buffer. (2) A "stale view" is still a prior full 2048-byte snapshot, not short. (3) No test passes b"" — every reward test builds bytes(2048)/bytearray(2048) (test_generic_reward_fallback.py:16, test_mario_checkpoint_reward.py:24). The production path trainer.py:3127->3176 feeds r.ram_snapshot and even indexes ram[0x006D]/[0x0086] on it at 3166 without failing, confirming the invariant.

Net: real defensive-hardening gap on a public PyO3 API, but no production or existing-test caller triggers it, and the named trigger classes are misreads/speculation. Any hit is a loud PanicException at the call site, not silent corruption. "medium" overstates a latent gap with no live trigger; corrected to "low".

finding.title: Audio render callback does lock().unwrap() inside the CoreAudio FFI frame — a poisoned mixer mutex becomes a hard SIGABRT of the whole process
finding.failure_scenario: `fill_callback` (audio.rs:426) runs on cpal's CoreAudio render thread, invoked from an extern "C" frame, and calls `state.lock().unwrap()`. If ANY thread panics while holding the mixer mutex (push_audio_i16 / push_audio_channels_i16 / set_instance_intensity all hold it across resample + ring operations, audio.rs:320-405), the mutex is poisoned and the very next audio callback's unwrap panics inside the FFI frame — unwinding across extern "C" aborts the process (SIGABRT). No Python traceback, no poison-save guard, no supervisor restart context: the GUI + training process vanishes mid-stream. The codebase already treats this exact hazard correctly elsewhere: pool.rs clear_pool_pace_target/pace_pool_step use `lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner())` (pool.rs:1476, 1492) specifically to never propagate poison.
finding.fix_sketch: Use the existing poison-recovering pattern for every `state.lock()` in audio.rs (fill_callback plus the AudioMixer methods at 256/281/289/300/320/366), and wrap fill_callback's body in `catch_unwind` that zero-fills `out` on any panic so the callback can never unwind into CoreAudio.

verdict.reasons:
The MECHANISM is accurate and verified: fill_callback (audio.rs:426) does state.lock().unwrap(), and it runs inside an extern "C" frame — cpal 0.15.3's macos backend has no catch_unwind, and coreaudio-rs 0.11.3 calls the Rust closure directly from `extern "C" fn input_proc` (render_callback.rs:758) with no catch_unwind, so a panic there would unwind across the FFI boundary and abort the process. The claim that the codebase defends against poison elsewhere is also true (pool.rs:1476/1492 use unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner())).

However, the FAILURE SCENARIO is overstated: it presupposes "ANY thread panics while holding the mixer mutex" to poison it, but no such panic is reachable in the current code. Every lock-holding section is panic-free under valid inputs: push_audio_i16/push_audio_channels_i16/set_instance_intensity index s.instances[instance_id] only after an `instance_id >= self.num_instances` early-return, and instances.len() is fixed to num_instances at construction with no resize path (index always in bounds); resample_linear's indexing is bounded (idx0<=n_src-2, idx1 capped by .min(n_src-1)); ring push/pop and the setters do no fallible ops; and fill_callback's own paths are guarded (Solo `idx < len`, drain_instance writes bounded by frames). Vec allocs abort rather than unwind on OOM, and release builds wrap on overflow. The only unwrap()s that panic on poison are the poison propagators themselves, and the PyO3-facing ones are caught by pyo3's catch_unwind (becoming Python exceptions, not aborts). So the mutex is effectively never poisoned and the abort chain has no reachable origin today.

This is a genuine latent hardening gap and an inconsistency with the rest of the codebase — worth the cheap fix (adopt the pool.rs poison-recovering pattern and/or wrap fill_callback's body in catch_unwind with a zero-fill fallback) — but it is not a live, firing crash path. Severity downgraded from medium to low: impact-if-triggered is high, but probability in the current code is essentially nil.

finding.title: Action receipts silently omit the random start-jitter noop steps, so honest-eval receipts do not self-replay
finding.failure_scenario: run_episode records into `_recorded` ONLY inside the control loop (line 671-674). The `start_jitter` noop pool steps (lines 650-652) execute BEFORE recording begins, and their count is a random draw `_rng.randint(0, start_jitter+1)` that is stored nowhere in the artifact. The sidecar meta (line 733) records `start_jitter` as the configured MAX and `steps` as `len(_recorded)` (post-jitter), not the drawn count. So for the documented flagship honest-eval config `eval_composite --sticky-prob 0.25 --start-jitter 16 --record-actions DIR` (decision_memo_2026-07-17.md:47), an episode that scores a seq_clear produces a receipt (`ep000_actions.npy`) that, replayed through the same harness from the same start-state (reset -> flush-noop -> feed actions), yields a trajectory phase-shifted by N unrecorded frames and a DIFFERENT outcome (often no clear). emit_fm2.py compounds it: it anchors at power-on (line 65) and plays actions with no jitter prefix at all. This directly falsifies the Tier-A 'even sticky episodes replay exactly / self-replay byte-compare' guarantee the campaign asserts for its published numbers.
finding.fix_sketch: Record the jitter steps into the receipt so the .npy is the complete stepped sequence from the start-state: in the jitter loop append `_recorded.append(0)` per noop (guarded by `record_dir is not None`), OR store the actual drawn jitter count in the meta sidecar and have every replay/emit_fm2 path prepend that many noops. Also add a self-replay assertion test with start_jitter>0 to the receipt test suite (currently only sticky is covered).

verdict.reasons:
The core mechanism is real and code-verified: in src/training/composite_policy.py the start_jitter noop steps (lines 650-652) run before recording and are never appended to _recorded; recording happens only inside the control loop (lines 671-674); the drawn count is _rng.randint(0, start_jitter+1) (line 651); and the meta sidecar (lines 733-739) stores the configured MAX (start_jitter=16) plus steps=len(_recorded), not the drawn count. emit_fm2.py (the only consumer of these RLDUTSBA-bitmask receipts; replay_to_demos.py consumes a different action-index format) anchors at power-on (line 65) and prepends no jitter. The flagship honest config `--sticky-prob 0.25 --start-jitter 16 --record-actions` is documented (decision_memo:47, campaign:435/643) and the campaign asserts "Receipts are Tier-A (self-replay, byte-compare)" (memo:74, campaign:648). I ran the exact RNG formula: the documented seed-0 honest episode draws 14 jitter noops, so replaying reset->flush->feed-actions (or emit_fm2 from power-on) is phase-shifted by 14 pool-steps and will not reproduce the recorded trajectory. So the asserted "all receipts self-replay" guarantee is genuinely violated for any jitter>0 receipt.

Severity is overstated at "high" for two reasons. (1) "Stored nowhere in the artifact" is false: the drawn count is the FIRST draw of RandomState((1_000_003*(seed+1))%2^32), and both seed and start_jitter are in the meta, so it is deterministically recoverable — a replay-side fix (recompute + prepend jitter) suffices and no artifact data is lost. (2) The specific "seq_clear receipt yields no clear / falsifies published numbers" scenario is mismatched to reality: the self-replay-VERIFIED "4514-mask, reproduces from power-on" receipt (campaign:648) comes from the DETERMINISTIC chain-gate (--stop-after-worlds 2, jitter 0), which is unaffected and replays correctly; the jitter-16 honest eval clears 0/50 on the W1 composite (campaign:436), so it produces only death receipts under metric (iii), which is explicitly "report-only, no threshold asserted." No headline/published clear number is falsified. The genuine harm is narrower than claimed: the unqualified Tier-A claim is false for jitter>0 receipts and those death receipts won't self-replay their recorded trajectory. Also, the parenthetical "(currently only sticky is covered)" in the fix sketch is inaccurate — there is NO receipt self-replay test at all; test_sticky_actions.py is a trainer _apply_sampled_actions test unrelated to composite receipts. Real defect worth fixing, but concrete impact is overstated: medium, not high.

finding.title: CompositeController._select raises an uncaught KeyError on an off-map level, aborting the entire multi-episode eval with no result row
finding.failure_scenario: `_select` raises KeyError when `resolve_level_key` returns None (no exact key, no `default`). It is called from the hysteresis level-switch branch (line 516). eval_composite.py wraps the whole episode loop (lines 228-240) in `try/finally` that only shuts the pool down; there is no `except`, and summarize()+the eval.jsonl append happen AFTER the loop. So if the agent reaches a level the manifest doesn't map, the KeyError unwinds through run_episode -> eval_composite -> main, killing the process: ALL episodes' results are lost and NO eval.jsonl row is written. Reachable two ways with a default-less manifest (the format documents `default` as optional): (1) `--stop-after-worlds 0` (the documented 'how far can it go' mode) — after clearing 1-4 the session continues into 2-1, hysteresis commits '2-1', KeyError; (2) honest-eval sticky/jitter pushes Mario into the 1-2 warp pipe -> world byte jumps to 4 -> hysteresis commits '4-1', KeyError. (Shipped configs currently include `default`, which masks this, but then mis-routes instead — see the seq_clear finding.)
finding.fix_sketch: Catch KeyError per-episode in eval_composite's loop and record a shaped 'off_map_level' episode result (with the reached label) instead of aborting; and/or have run_episode end the episode cleanly with end_reason='off_map' when `_select` can't resolve. Either way one bad episode must not discard the other N-1 and the log row.

verdict.reasons: The crash mechanism is real and correctly traced, but the scenario overstates reachability. CONFIRMED parts: composite_policy.py:460 `_select` raises KeyError when resolve_level_key returns None (no @area key, no exact label, no "default"); it is invoked from observe's hysteresis branch (516), the area-change branch (557), and begin (474); observe runs in run_episode's loop (line 693) with no try/except; eval_composite.py's episode loop (228-240) sits in a try whose only handler is `finally: pool.shutdown()` (no except), and summarize()+the eval.jsonl append (244, 282-283) are after the loop; main() (328) has no try/except. So a mid-episode KeyError does unwind out to process exit, discarding the local `records` list and writing no log row — a genuine eval-integrity failure. OVERSTATED parts: (1) both stated reachability paths require a default-less manifest that also omits the reached level, and ALL shipped manifests include `default` — composite_scout.yaml, composite_world1.yaml, composite_learned.yaml — so the KeyError cannot fire under any shipped config (it mis-routes instead, a separate finding). (2) Path 2 (1-2 warp -> world 4 -> "4-1") would not even fire on composite_world1.yaml, which explicitly maps 4-1/4-3/2-1/3-1; and composite_learned.yaml has default. (3) The raise is partly intended: resolve_level_key's None branch is documented "the caller fails loud rather than silently reusing the wrong specialist." The true, fixable defect is the blast radius (whole-batch abort + lost log row) not the raise itself. Because triggering requires a user-authored default-less manifest AND reaching an unmapped level — a documented-but-non-shipped shape — the practical risk is lower than medium; corrected to low.

finding.title: seq_clear / worlds_cleared latch on ANY castle clear with no world or warp guard, so a warp-then-castle-clear is reported as a sequential World-1 clear
finding.failure_scenario: SequentialTracker.update sets `_seq_clear=True` (and increments `_worlds_cleared`) on ANY world-byte increment whose prev displayed level was the x-4 castle (lines 152-157) — it never checks that the crossing left World 1, and `_warp_taken` is an independent latch that does not veto `_seq_clear`. summarize() then computes `seq_clear_rate = sum(r['seq_clear'])/n` (composite_policy.py:807) with NO `and not warp_taken` guard, and eval_game.py both tallies and BREAKS the episode on `tracker.seq_clear` (lines 481, 494). Under the honest-eval protocol (whose whole purpose is to push the agent off-trajectory), an episode that warps out of 1-2 to World 4 (warp_taken=True) and then clears a World-4 castle latches seq_clear=True and is counted in the headline seq_clear_rate as a genuine sequential World-1 clear. The same missing guard makes _per_level_breakdown (composite_policy.py:757) count exit_reason 'advanced' as 'cleared' for a segment the agent WARPED out of (a warp out of 1-2 has _label_rank rising, reason='advanced' at line 506), inflating per-level clear counts for levels that were never actually cleared.
finding.fix_sketch: Gate the castle-clear branch on `self._prev_world == 0` (a real 1-4->2-1 crossing) for the World-1 seq_clear, and/or expose `seq_clear and not warp_taken` and use that in summarize's seq_clear_rate and eval_game's tally. In _per_level_breakdown, distinguish a warp exit (consult the tracker's warp latch / world-jump magnitude) from a genuine forward clear before counting 'advanced' as 'cleared'.

verdict.reasons: Code reading confirms the defect at every cited location. smb_sequential.py:152-157 sets _seq_clear/_worlds_cleared on ANY world-byte increment out of an x-4 castle display, with no check that the crossing left World 1 (no `_prev_world==0` guard) — directly violating the property docstring at line 176 ("crossing into World 2"). _warp_taken is set on an independent branch (line 157) and never vetoes _seq_clear. Grep across both consumers confirms no `and not warp` guard exists anywhere: composite_policy.py:807 (seq_clear_rate), :702/:711/:715 (worlds_cleared break + record), and eval_game.py:481/:494 (break + tally) all latch on the unguarded seq_clear/worlds_cleared. The stated scenario genuinely fires: warping out of 1-2 only sets _warp_taken (episode continues since the warp isn't a castle exit), and a later World-4 castle clear (4-4, world byte 3->4 with _prev_display==3) then latches _seq_clear=True and is counted in seq_clear_rate as a sequential World-1 clear. The secondary claim is also confirmed: _label_rank("4-1")=(4,1) > (1,2)=_label_rank("1-2"), so a warp out of 1-2 marks the departed segment exit_reason="advanced" (line 507), which _per_level_breakdown line 757 counts as "cleared", inflating per-level clears for a level the agent warped out of (this composite path additionally needs a manifest net/default for the warp-destination world or it crashes at _select instead). Severity kept at medium rather than raised: this is the headline go/no-go gate metric and the project treats eval integrity as non-negotiable, and the fix is a one-line guard — but the primary seq_clear false positive requires the agent to also clear an entire untrained later world, which is extremely unlikely for the World-1-campaign agents being gated, and warp_rate is separately reported so an analyst could catch it manually. Real, unguarded, and confirmed; practical trigger frequency is low, so medium (not high) is right.

finding.title: _gx_pad is not cleared on a committed hysteresis level switch, leaking stale noop actions into the incoming specialist
finding.failure_scenario: When a level switch commits, the branch resets `_gx_stage` and `_gx_confirm` (lines 514-515) but the else-branch (lines 524-527, taken when the new level's entry noop_pad==0) never sets `self._gx_pad = 0`. If an in-level gx-stage pad was still pending (e.g. 2-1's `gx_switches: noop_pad: 1` in composite_world1.yaml) when the level byte auto-advances during those noop frames (a flagpole/auto-walk seam) and hysteresis commits into a level with no entry pad (1-1..1-4 have none), the leftover positive `_gx_pad` persists. act() then keeps returning noop (line 488) for the incoming specialist's first frames and observe re-runs the mid-pad reset (lines 565-573), so the measured trajectory contains agent actions the policy never chose and the incoming net's stack seeds several frames late — a measurement-fidelity corruption in exactly the gx-routed seams the campaign leans on.
finding.fix_sketch: In the level-switch commit branch set `self._gx_pad = 0` before the `if _pad > 0` check (the level switch is authoritative over any in-flight gx-stage pad). Add a state-machine test that fires a hysteresis switch while `_gx_pad>0` and asserts the incoming net's first act() is its own action, not a leaked noop.

verdict.reasons: The code observation is accurate: the level-switch commit else-branch (src/training/composite_policy.py:526-529, taken when the incoming level's noop_pad==0) sets adapter/obs/hidden but does NOT reset self._gx_pad, while the sibling `if _pad > 0` branch (522-525) overwrites it. So a missing reset is genuinely present as a latent hygiene gap. But the described failure scenario cannot fire under any shipped config, and the cited example is self-contradictory: (1) In composite_world1.yaml the only gx-routed level is 2-1 (gx_switches at gx1440, noop_pad:1), and 2-1 advances to 2-2, which itself has `entry: noop_pad: 1` — so a 2-1->2-2 commit takes the OVERWRITE branch (522-525), never the buggy else-branch. 2-1 never advances into 1-1..1-4 ("which have none") in normal play. (2) In composite_learned.yaml, 2-1's gx switch has NO noop_pad (defaults to 0), so _gx_pad is never set >0 there — nothing to leak. Grep confirms 2-1 is the ONLY level with gx_switches in any config; there is no shipped config where a gx-padded level's successor is a no-pad level. (3) Timing forecloses co-occurrence: run order is act->step->observe (lines 667-693); the gx switch sets _gx_pad=1 only in the last observe branch (596) reached MID-LEVEL (2-1 seam gx1440; flag gx3299), and with noop_pad=1 the pad is decremented to 0 on the very next observe (565-574). For the level-switch branch (504) to preempt that single alive-frame, hysteresis (k=2) would have to commit a level transition at gx1440 — nowhere near a level boundary — so no commit coincides. Net: the missing reset is a real defensive-hardening item (a future config with a gx switch near an auto-advance seam feeding a no-pad successor could trip it), but the "active corruption in exactly the gx-routed seams the campaign leans on" claim is overstated and unreachable today. Downgrade medium -> low.

finding.title: RustPool `seed` is a dead knob — eval_composite --seed never reaches the emulator, so logged `seed` overstates reproducibility control
finding.failure_scenario: RustPool.__init__ stores `self._seed = seed` (line 98) but start() constructs `nes_core.Pool(rom_path, num_workers, frame_skip, start_state_path)` (lines 151-156) and never passes it — and nes_core.Pool's constructor has no seed parameter at all (pool.rs:640-648). eval_composite.py passes `--seed` into `RustPool(..., seed=seed)` (line 224) and stamps `result['seed']=seed` as a self-describing protocol field (line 251), and also calls torch.manual_seed(seed) which is inert for greedy argmax. So the emulator/torch seeding is a no-op: two runs differing only in --seed yield byte-identical emulator trajectories, while the logged `seed` field implies a control that does not exist. This is the exact 'parsed-but-dead knob' class flagged in the audit priors (eval --start-state, sticky_action_prob). Impact is bounded — the sticky/jitter reproducibility that actually varies runs IS correctly seeded via the per-episode `_rng` (composite_policy.py:643) from the same seed — but the field is misleading for anyone auditing a logged row's provenance.
finding.fix_sketch: Either wire the seed through to a real emulator RNG (if power-on RAM / DMC randomization is ever exercised) or, since eval always warm-starts from a fixed save-state, drop the dead `seed=` parameter from RustPool and stop logging a `seed` that only governs the Python sticky/jitter RNG — or rename the logged field to make clear it seeds only the stochastic-eval RNG, not the emulator.

verdict.reasons: Factual core CONFIRMED: RustPool stores self._seed at rust_pool_adapter.py:98 and (grep-verified) reads it nowhere; start() at lines 151-156 never passes it to nes_core.Pool; nes_core.Pool::new (pool.rs:640-648) has no seed parameter at all; eval_composite.py:223 passes seed= to RustPool, :121 calls torch.manual_seed(seed) which is inert because act()->forward_greedy uses torch.argmax (composite_policy.py:289); :251 logs result['seed']. The sticky/jitter _rng at composite_policy.py:643 IS correctly seeded from seed (via seed*10_000+_ep, eval :238). So the RustPool seed= arg and torch.manual_seed are genuinely dead. HOWEVER the eval-integrity framing is overstated: this eval warm-starts from a fixed save-state (deterministic emulator, no power-on RAM/DMC randomness to seed) with a greedy-argmax policy, so the ONLY source of run-to-run variation is sticky/jitter, which the logged seed correctly and completely governs. Re-running with the same seed/sticky_prob/start_jitter reproduces byte-identical results, so the logged seed is a faithful reproducibility key, not a misleading one — the 'overstates reproducibility control / misleading provenance' claim does not hold. The 'byte-identical trajectories regardless of --seed' scenario is true only when sticky=0 and jitter=0, exactly the case where the seed has nothing to control and logging it is harmless. This is a real dead-parameter/code-clarity smell (a maintainer could mistake seed= for an emulator knob), not an eval-integrity break; reproducibility is intact. Downgrade medium -> low.
